label: map_1
name: Experimenting Causal Program Library
mech: The system keeps a growing library of small probabilistic programs, each encoding a candidate causal mechanism (e.g., "pressure causes leak if seal is worn"). When several programs explain the observations equally well, it computes which intervention (real action, simulator query or tool call) would best tell them apart, runs it, and reweights or deletes programs based on the result. New programs are synthesized by recombining fragments of programs that survived, so the library compresses over time.
value: It can discover and reliably use real cause-and-effect structure, including in situations that never appeared in its data.

label: map_1
name: Self-Revising Provenance Belief Ledger
mech: Every assertion the system adopts becomes a node in a persistent graph that stores its source, confidence and the nodes it was derived from. On each inference step a constraint checker scans for contradictions. Conflicts are resolved by retracting the least-supported justification, and the retraction automatically propagates to all dependent conclusions (truth maintenance). Generation is restricted to drawing on the active ledger and has to cite node IDs.
value: It enables lifelong learning without catastrophic forgetting, with traceable reasoning and instant correction of any fact and everything derived from it.

label: map_1
name: Information-Priced Compute Market
mech: Many heterogeneous modules (search, simulation, symbolic solvers, small neural nets) bid for slices of a shared compute budget. A bid is priced by the expected reduction in task uncertainty, and the payout is the realized reduction. Modules that bid well gain budget and get copied with mutations, while chronically bad bidders are retired. The architecture is therefore an evolving economy rather than a fixed graph.
value: It makes possible adaptive, open-ended allocation of reasoning effort and self-directed architectural growth after deployment.

label: map_2
name: Audited Sleep Consolidation
mech: Surprising experiences go verbatim into a fast episodic buffer. During offline phases the system replays them to propose weight deltas inside a sandboxed copy of its slow network. Each delta is accepted only if a self-maintained regression suite of past skills shows no loss, and rejected deltas are stored as interference records that shape later proposals.
value: It enables continual lifelong learning after deployment without catastrophic forgetting.

label: map_2
name: Evolving Executable World Simulators
mech: The system maintains a population of small probabilistic programs, each a candidate simulator of some part of the environment. Queries are answered by running or intervening on the best-scoring simulators. Prediction errors drive program-synthesis mutations, and simulators are selected by how well they compress observations and predict accurately.
value: It gives explicit causal and counterfactual reasoning and lets the system discover new models that can be inspected.

label: map_2
name: Verified Competence Cartography
mech: An embedding-indexed map stores the system's ground-truth-verified error statistics for each region of problem space, updated whenever an outcome is checked. Before answering, the system looks up the query's region. It then answers, abstains, asks for information, or routes the region to the learning loop, depending on the measured reliability and the cost of being wrong.
value: It gives reliable self-knowledge of where the system is competent, so it can abstain and direct its own learning based on its actual track record.

label: map_3
name: Surprise-Gated Synaptic Patch Memory
mech: When prediction error on an input crosses a learned threshold, the system writes a small key-value module next to the frozen core. The key is the context embedding and the value is a low-rank change to the core's weights. Those changes take effect only when a later context is similar to that key. During an offline phase, the system replays old episodes against the patches. It merges patches that do the same thing and deletes ones that conflict, using how often they agree as the score. Each patch keeps a count of how often it was used and how often it was confirmed, and patches that stop earning their place are removed.
value: The system could learn permanently from a single experience without forgetting what it already knows or needing retraining.

label: map_3
name: Falsifiable Causal World-Graph
mech: Perception updates a running graph of objects, their attributes and typed causal links. Each link carries a probability and a count of how many times its predictions came true. Before each step the system simulates what it expects to observe, then compares that with what it actually observes. When they differ, it traces the error back through the graph to the links most to blame and revises them: it adds hidden variables, splits links or reverses their direction. It can also run interventions inside the graph to test competing explanations before acting.
value: The system could know when its beliefs are wrong, reason about counterfactuals, and keep a consistent, inspectable model of the world over long periods.

label: map_3
name: Verifier-Halted Constraint Relaxation
mech: A query is turned into a set of variables, which are partial answers and sub-goals, plus constraints between them that are learned or extracted from the query. Local update rules pass messages between these units, and the system keeps iterating until either a symbolic checker or a learned checker confirms that every constraint is met, or the energy of the system stops falling. When progress stalls, the system adds intermediate variables, for example lemmas or sub-plans, and stores successful arrangements as reusable templates.
value: The system could spend compute in proportion to how hard a problem is and solve multi-step problems it cannot solve in one pass, with a clear signal for when it has succeeded and when it has failed.

label: g1_neg
name: Fully reversible uncomputable inference
mech: Every layer and every reasoning step is a bijection, built from invertible couplings with explicit "garbage" registers, so each output can be run backward exactly to the inputs and training examples that produced it. Learning is done as reversible updates that are logged as compact inverse operations. To forget a datum, or to undo a conclusion, the system uncomputes the matching update chain instead of retraining. Nothing is erased irreversibly, so in principle the system also runs near the thermodynamic limit.
value: Exact, verifiable unlearning and bit-level provenance for any output, which approximate gradient-based models cannot give.

label: g1_neg
name: Teach-to-retain transmission bottleneck
mech: A capability counts as kept only if the system can write a short, human-readable lesson that lets a fresh, small, randomly initialized student reach the same behavior within a fixed budget of examples. Anything that cannot be transmitted this way is pruned on each generation cycle, and the surviving lessons become the next generation's training core (iterated cultural learning). The system adapts by changing what it teaches, not by refining a model of the world.
value: Knowledge becomes explicit, portable and auditable by design, and opaque shortcuts that cannot be taught are removed systematically.

label: g1_neg
name: Phase-interference evidence aggregation
mech: Every derivation path to a candidate answer contributes a complex amplitude, and the path's phase is set by the assumptions it relies on. Paths that support an answer through incompatible assumptions cancel each other out, while paths that agree reinforce each other. The final confidence is the squared magnitude after summing. The phase assignments are learned, so that recurring conflicting assumption pairs become orthogonal or opposed.
value: The system can represent "many reasons that cancel out" as real uncertainty, which averaging probabilities cannot express, so it stops being overconfident when it has many weak, conflicting justifications.

label: g1_core
name: Guarded Trace Compilation of Skills
mech: A slow, general deliberative solver handles new problems and records the step trace it executes. When a trace becomes hot, it is compiled into a fast specialized routine with explicit guard predicates, which are the input conditions the trace assumed. At runtime, a failed guard falls back to the solver and increments a counter on that exit. An exit that keeps failing is compiled into its own child trace, so the trace tree grows and existing traces are never overwritten.
value: The system gains new skills from a few experiences, with no gradient retraining and no forgetting, because old traces stay intact behind their guards.

label: g1_core
name: Kinetic Proofreading Inference
mech: A candidate inference step must survive K sequential, irreversible holding stages before it is committed. At each stage it is re-tested for match against an independently perturbed context, and if it detaches it resets to the beginning rather than to the previous stage. Errors therefore decay roughly as f^K. The number of stages a candidate survives gives a confidence score, and the system can raise K wherever stakes are high.
value: Reasoning accuracy can be bought with compute in a predictable, near-exponential way, instead of being capped by a single forward pass.

label: g1_core
name: Learned Dimensional Similarity Algebra
mech: Every latent quantity carries a learned vector of integer "dimension" exponents. These are inferred so that every observed relation is dimensionally homogeneous, by keeping the dimension matrix's integer nullspace consistent across relations. Learned laws are stored only as functions of the dimensionless groups the Pi theorem derives from that matrix. When no consistent assignment exists, the system takes it as a sign of a missing hidden quantity and introduces one.
value: A relation learned in one regime transfers exactly to unseen scales and configurations that share the same dimensionless groups.

label: g1_gap
name: Perturbation-Signature Variable Extraction
mech: Closes G1. The system does not parse the input directly. It applies a large set of small edits to the raw input (swapping a token or phrase, inpainting an image patch, shifting time) and records how each edit changes a frozen predictor's output distribution. Edits are clustered by their effect signature, and each cluster becomes one variable whose values are the observed edit outcomes. A typed link is added wherever a pair of clusters shows a non-additive second-order effect, meaning editing both does not equal the sum of editing each. The edit library and clusters are stored, and the clustering is refit as new inputs come in, so the structured form is built from the input itself rather than hand-specified.
value: It turns "parse the input into the representation" into a measurable procedure that works the same way on text, pixels and sensor streams.

label: g1_gap
name: Planted-Twin Correctness Oracle
mech: Closes G2. For each real task type, the system builds twin tasks in the easy direction, where the answer is fixed first and the problem is generated from it: run a program and then ask for its output, hide a known span and then ask to reconstruct it, compose a plan and then ask what goal it achieves. A discriminator is trained adversarially until it cannot tell the twins from real tasks. The system stores per-twin-cluster accuracy for every checker and solver. On a real task with no oracle, the correctness estimate is the measured accuracy on the twins that match it most closely.
value: It gives a calibrated, always-available correctness signal on tasks where no verified outcome will ever arrive.

label: g1_gap
name: Shared False-Alarm Wealth Thresholds
mech: Closes G4. Every cutoff (surprise, "similar enough", "least-supported", stopping tolerance) is replaced by an online conformal p-value. The p-value is computed against a null distribution built from shuffled, time-reversed or context-permuted copies of the system's own recent data stream. All thresholds draw on one global error budget using alpha-investing. Each test spends some of that budget to fire, and it earns budget back when a firing is later confirmed useful by downstream prediction gain, so cutoffs tighten or loosen automatically as conditions change. The stored state is only the per-test null samples and the current wealth balance.
value: Behavior that used to depend on hand-tuned constants becomes self-calibrating with a guaranteed bound on the total false-alarm rate, including in a new domain with no history.

label: g1_mech
name: Interference-Carved Resonance Grid
mech: Candidate partial answers are injected as phase-coded waves into a grid of oscillating cells. Contradictory candidates get opposite phase and cancel, while mutually consistent ones reinforce into standing peaks. Cells that repeatedly hold strong amplitude stiffen, cutting lasting channels that bias future propagation. The stable peak pattern is read out as the answer.
value: Many alternatives can be searched at the same time, with inconsistency removed physically rather than candidate by candidate.

label: g1_mech
name: Rescaling-Tested Kind Exponents
mech: Every internal quantity carries an exponent vector over a growing set of base kinds, and operations may only combine compatible vectors. The system keeps rescaling or swapping kinds in its own inputs and checks that its outputs change exactly as the exponents predict. Each failure splits a kind, adds a new one, or revises an exponent.
value: Reliable extrapolation far beyond the magnitudes in its experience, plus automatic detection of answers that make no sense.

label: g1_mech
name: Teach-Back Transfer Gap
mech: Knowledge is also held as short, explicit lessons. Periodically a small, empty student is rebuilt using only those lessons and scored on held-out cases. Lessons linked to the student's failures are rewritten or split, and lessons whose removal leaves the score unchanged are deleted. The size of the gap between the system's accuracy and the student's drives the rewriting.
value: Unspoken, unexplainable competence becomes explicit, checkable knowledge that can be passed on, so the system knows which of its skills it actually understands.

label: g1_loop
name: Rigidity-Braced Concept Frames
mech: Concepts are joints and learned relations are bars. The system periodically computes the spectrum of the rigidity matrix. Floppy modes trigger acquisition of new bracing relations, and self-stress states split the node along the eigenvector of the stress. The concept frame is stored, and it grows or splits as these spectral tests fire.
value: The system can find for itself which concepts are underdetermined and which are conflated, and repair them.

label: g1_loop
name: Allan-Grown Memory Timescales
mech: The system computes the Allan deviation of its prediction residuals across context lag. When the deviation rises at τ\*, it creates a new recurrent state with time constant τ\*. It keeps that state only if the rise in deviation flattens afterwards.
value: Memory gets exactly the timescales that the data's hidden drift requires.

label: g1_loop
name: Wahlund-Split Module Growth
mech: For each module, the system tests whether paired feature co-activations match the products of their marginal frequencies. A heterozygote-like deficit indicates two pooled subpopulations, so the module splits in two, inputs are assigned by admixture inference, and a router is learned. Over time, splits build a lineage tree of specialized modules.
value: The architecture adds specialists when a statistic shows a module has been mixing two input types.
